articles.title: Installing 12 m Street Light Poles Without a Crane: Specification Boundaries and Project Review
articles.seoTitle: 12m Street Light Pole Installation Without Crane | velolev
articles.description: Specification-grounded engineering overview for installing 12 m street light poles without a mobile crane: 300 kg rated load, 85 kg two-module layout, 180–260 mm flange span, and project review boundaries.

sections.heading: Overview
paragraphs: Erecting municipal and solar street light columns has traditionally relied on mobile cranes or boom trucks. On narrow urban sidewalks, pedestrian corridors, landscaped medians, and unpaved solar project sites, bringing a heavy crane vehicle into position can create access, ground-bearing, and traffic-control constraints. Project engineers therefore evaluate whether a portable hydraulic pole lifter can be used instead of a crane for standard 12 m class lighting poles.

Key Specification Boundaries for Project Review:
- **Applicable Pole Class:** Listed for 12 m light poles, subject to total assembled pole weight, center of gravity, and site review.
- **Rated Load Limit:** 300 kg maximum rated load on the product specification sheet.
- **Two-Module Architecture:** 85 kg total equipment weight split into a 45 kg hydraulic lifting module and a 40 kg 24 V electrical cabinet, with 1–2 operators listed on the sheet.
- **Flange and Anchor Bolt Scope:** 180–260 mm flange hole span shown with M16–M24 anchor bolt sizes listed; non-standard bases require a dimensioned drawing review.

sections.heading: 1. Site Access and Project Factors When Evaluating Crane-Free Pole Installation
paragraphs: Raising a 12 m street light pole from horizontal to vertical places bending and overturning reactions at the pole base and foundation anchor bolts. Unlike a crane boom suspended from above, a portable hydraulic pole lifter works at ground level by connecting to the pole base arrangement and anchoring to the existing foundation bolts.

Matching a 12 m pole height alone does not confirm suitability. Before selecting crane-free installation, project teams need to review the complete assembled weight of the pole, luminaire, bracket arm and solar components, the foundation condition, overhead utility clearances, and local site safety rules.

sections.heading: 2. Two-Module Hydraulic Architecture and Listed Specifications
paragraphs: The velolev portable light pole jack is organized into two separate modules powered by an onboard 24 V rechargeable battery rather than an external grid connection or diesel generator.

According to the current product specification sheet:
- **Hydraulic Lifting Module:** 610 × 220 × 220 mm; weight: 45 kg (hydraulic cylinder, hydraulic valve, oil pump, and oil pressure gauge).
- **Electrical Cabinet:** 500 × 300 × 250 mm; weight: 40 kg (control system, hydraulic pump, 24 V rechargeable battery, ammeter, voltage meter, and lift buttons).
- **Total Equipment Weight and Packaging:** 85 kg total equipment weight; 650 × 350 × 500 mm source-sheet packaging dimensions.
- **Operators Listed:** 1–2 operators listed on the specification sheet; site crew allocation must follow project safety and manual-handling rules.

The specification sheet also lists manufacturer-reported figures of 20 s lift time, over 50 lifts per full charge, and more than 3000 usage cycles. Field validation for test load, site conditions, timing method, and repeatability remains pending, so these figures serve as specification labels rather than guaranteed field cycle times or service life.

sections.heading: 3. Base Flange Span, Anchor Bolts, and Standard Included Configuration
paragraphs: Compatibility at the pole base depends on the flange geometry, bolt circle span, stud diameter, and thread projection above the concrete foundation.

The specification sheet records separate figures for listed compatibility and default included hardware:
- **Flange Hole Span Shown:** 180–260 mm on the source diagram. Because the flange diagram includes dimension terminology that still requires engineering clarification, final connection details must be reviewed for the actual project.
- **Anchor Bolt Sizes Listed:** M16, M18, M20, M22, and M24.
- **Standard Included Configuration:** 1 equipment set, 4 sets each of M16, M18, M20, and M22 anchor bolts, and 1 set of ground stakes. M24 is listed in the compatibility table but is not included by default.
- **Non-Standard Bases:** Non-standard bases require a dimensioned drawing review before confirming fitment.

sections.heading: 4. Pre-Installation Engineering Checks and Operating Review Boundaries
paragraphs: Detailed step-by-step field operating sequences are currently held for engineering review rather than published as a universal site operating procedure. Every installation must follow site-specific electrical safety clearances, foundation inspection checks, and local lifting regulations.

sections.heading: Pre-Lift Foundation and Airspace Checks
paragraphs: Before mobilizing equipment to site, confirm that the concrete foundation has been inspected and approved by the responsible engineer, that anchor bolt threads and projections are clean and undamaged, and that the full 12 m arc of the pole remains safely clear of overhead power lines and adjacent structures.

sections.heading: Equipment Connection and Ground-Level Pre-Assembly
paragraphs: Verify that the hydraulic module and 24 V electrical cabinet are inspected prior to lifting, that hydraulic hoses and electrical connections are properly seated, and that luminaire wiring and bracket assembly are checked at ground level before raising the column.

sections.heading: Controlled Lift and Final Bolt Tightening
paragraphs: During elevation, keep personnel clear of the swing path and pinch points while monitoring base alignment and plumbness. Once the pole reaches vertical alignment, secure and tighten the structural anchor nuts according to the project specification before disconnecting the lifting assembly.

sections.heading: 5. Boundary Conditions: When a Mobile Crane Is Still Required
paragraphs: A portable hydraulic pole lifter is designed for light-duty 12 m class columns within its 300 kg rated load and 180–260 mm flange span. It is not a universal substitute for a mobile crane.

Use a mobile crane or alternative approved lifting method when any of the following conditions apply:
1. **Total Assembled Weight Exceeds 300 kg:** Heavy decorative columns, thick-walled poles, or multi-luminaire and large solar battery assemblies above the 300 kg rated load.
2. **Pole Height Exceeds 12 m:** High-mast columns or tall roadway poles beyond the listed 12 m class.
3. **Unreviewed Flange or Foundation Geometry:** Bases outside the 180–260 mm hole span, bolts outside M16–M24, or non-standard bases that have not passed a dimensioned drawing review.
4. **Adverse Weather or Compromised Footings:** High wind conditions on site or damaged foundations and anchor studs that cannot safely carry erection reactions.

sections.heading: What are the rated pole height and load limits?
paragraphs: The specification sheet lists a 12 m applicable pole class and a 300 kg rated load. Both limits, along with the pole center of gravity and flange geometry, must be checked for each project. Columns heavier than 300 kg or taller than 12 m require a crane.

sections.heading: How many operators are listed on the specification sheet?
paragraphs: The specification sheet lists 1–2 operators for the 85 kg two-module system (45 kg hydraulic module and 40 kg electrical cabinet). Actual crew size on site must follow your project safety plan and manual-handling rules.

sections.heading: Which anchor bolts are included and what if my flange is non-standard?
paragraphs: The specification sheet lists M16, M18, M20, M22, and M24 anchor bolts across a 180–260 mm flange hole span. Standard delivery includes 4 sets each of M16, M18, M20, and M22; M24 is not included by default. Non-standard bases require a dimensioned drawing review.

sections.heading: How is the equipment powered on sites without grid electricity?
paragraphs: The electrical cabinet uses a 24 V rechargeable battery, requiring no external mains supply or generator during lifting. The sheet lists manufacturer-reported figures of over 50 lifts per full charge and 20 s lift time, with field validation still pending.

articles.title: M24 Anchor Bolts and 180–260 mm Flange Span Compatibility on a Portable Pole Lifter
articles.description: Engineering compatibility guide for M24 anchor studs, 180–260 mm flange hole spans, standard M16–M22 included bolts, and drawing review rules for non-standard pole bases.

sections.heading: Direct Compatibility Answer
paragraphs: The velolev Portable Light Pole Lifter specification sheet lists M16, M18, M20, M22, and M24 anchor bolt sizes alongside a 180–260 mm flange hole span. However, listed compatibility and default included hardware are separate items: standard delivery includes 4 sets each of M16, M18, M20, and M22 anchor bolts, while M24 hardware is not included by default.

In addition, because the source flange diagram contains dimension terminology that still requires engineering clarification, teams must verify how their drawing defines the span and submit a dimensioned base-plate drawing whenever M24 studs, 6-hole or 8-hole patterns, or spans outside 180–260 mm are specified.

sections.heading: 1. Standard Included Bolts (M16–M22) vs M24 and Non-Standard Flanges
paragraphs: Procurement and site teams frequently assume that every bolt diameter printed in a specification table ships in the standard crate. Separating standard delivery hardware from project-reviewed items prevents last-minute site delays.

| Flange or Bolt Parameter | Source Sheet Listing | Standard Delivery Scope | Engineering Review Requirement |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| M16, M18, M20, M22 anchor bolts | Listed in M16–M24 compatibility table | Included (4 sets per size) | Confirm thread projection and drawing span definition |
| M24 anchor bolts | Listed in M16–M24 compatibility table | Not included in standard delivery | Flag M24 in inquiry; confirm hardware scope and drawing |
| 4-hole base within 180–260 mm span | Listed in quick-check envelope | Standard 4-bolt pattern reference | Verify whether drawing measures hole span or bolt circle |
| 6-hole or 8-hole base pattern | Outside default 4-hole check | Not covered by default kit | Non-standard bases require a dimensioned drawing review |
| Span below 180 mm or above 260 mm | Outside listed 180–260 mm range | Not covered by default kit | Non-standard bases require a dimensioned drawing review |

sections.heading: 2. Why Flange Hole Span Terminology Must Be Checked Against Drawings
paragraphs: On street lighting foundation drawings, engineers may dimension a base plate by opposite-hole span, adjacent-hole spacing, or pitch circle diameter. On the current source specification sheet, the flange diagram includes dimension terminology that still requires engineering clarification before it can be treated as a standalone fitment guarantee.

Rather than assuming that a 240 mm or 250 mm callout on a tender sheet matches automatically, attach the dimensioned pole-base drawing showing bolt diameter, hole count, hole-to-hole geometry, and stud projection above the concrete footing. Non-standard bases require a dimensioned drawing review, and custom transition hardware is never promised without engineering evaluation.

sections.heading: 3. Pre-Inquiry Base Plate Checklist for M24 and Custom Projects
paragraphs:
Before submitting a quotation request for a project using M24 anchor studs or non-standard base plates, compile the following four items so the connection can be reviewed accurately:
1. **Dimensioned Flange Drawing:** Provide hole count (4, 6, or 8 holes), exact hole diameter, and clearly labeled hole-to-hole dimensions.
2. **Anchor Bolt Specification:** State thread diameter (for example, M24), exposed thread length above the foundation, and nut/washer arrangement.
3. **Assembled Column Envelope:** Confirm total assembled pole weight (up to 300 kg rated load) and pole height (12 m class).
4. **Foundation Inspection Status:** Confirm that the concrete footing and embedded studs have been inspected and approved by the responsible site engineer.

sections.heading: Frequently Asked Questions on M24 and 180–260 mm Flanges
paragraphs: **Are M24 anchor bolts included in the standard velolev kit?** No. Standard delivery includes 1 equipment set, 1 set of ground stakes, and 4 sets each of M16, M18, M20, and M22 anchor bolts. M24 appears in the compatibility table but must be confirmed separately.

**Can a 6-hole flange with a 220 mm span use the standard 4-bolt setup?** No. Any 6-hole or 8-hole base plate, as well as any span below 180 mm or above 260 mm, is classified as a non-standard base and requires a dimensioned drawing review before confirming fitment.

articles.title: Solar Street Light Pole Weight Limits: Checking Panel, Bracket, and Battery Loads Under 300 kg
articles.seoTitle: Solar Street Light Pole Weight Limits Under 300kg | velolev
articles.description: How to calculate total assembled solar street light weight (pole, solar panel, mounting bracket, battery box, and luminaire) against the 300 kg rated load and 12 m class limit.

sections.heading: Why Bare-Pole Weight Is Insufficient for Solar Lighting Projects
paragraphs: Off-grid solar street light columns carry significantly more top-mounted mass than standard grid-connected roadway poles. When contractors check only the bare steel pole weight against the velolev Portable Light Pole Lifter 300 kg rated load and 12 m applicable pole class, they risk overlooking solar panels, mounting frames, battery enclosures, and outreach brackets.

While the equipment is powered by an onboard 24 V rechargeable battery and requires no grid electricity on rural corridors, lifting a complete solar assembly has not yet been validated as a standard configuration. Every solar street light project must therefore undergo an assembled weight, geometry, and base-drawing review before selecting crane-free installation.

sections.heading: 1. Assembled Solar Pole Weight Audit Table
paragraphs: Before submitting a solar lighting brief, add every component that will be attached to the column during the lift. If the combined total exceeds 300 kg or the overall height exceeds the 12 m class, a mobile crane is required.

| Solar Pole Sub-Assembly | What to Measure for the Lift Audit | Impact on 300 kg / 12 m Boundary |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Tapered or octagonal pole shaft | Bare structural column mass and overall length | Must remain within 12 m class and leave margin for top hardware |
| Solar photovoltaic module(s) | Panel mass, frame weight, and mounting elevation | Adds top-end mass and shifts the center of gravity upward |
| Top mounting frame and outreach arm | Steel bracket, tilt frame, and luminaire arm mass | Must be summed into the 300 kg rated load ceiling |
| Battery enclosure and controller | Pole-mounted battery box and charge controller weight | Often the single heaviest accessory on off-grid columns |
| LED luminaire(s) and internal cabling | Single or twin luminaires, harnesses, and fasteners | Include all pre-wired components lifted together |

sections.heading: 2. 24 V Battery Power vs Pending Solar Assembly Validation
paragraphs: On remote highway and rural electrification corridors, the 24 V rechargeable battery inside the 40 kg electrical cabinet eliminates the need for site mains power or a separate generator during lifting. The specification sheet lists a manufacturer-reported figure of over 50 lifts per full charge and a 20 s lift time, with field validation still pending.

Because top-heavy solar panels and battery boxes alter load distribution and wind exposure compared with a conventional luminaire-only pole, the current specification sheet treats complete solar assemblies as pending project-specific validation rather than an automatic standard configuration.

sections.heading: 3. Required Engineering Submittal for Solar Pole Projects
paragraphs:
To evaluate whether your off-grid solar lighting package fits within equipment limits, include four items in your project inquiry:
- **Complete Assembly Weight Sheet:** Itemized weights for the pole shaft, solar panel(s), bracket, battery box, and luminaire, plus the verified total assembled weight.
- **Elevation and Mounting Drawing:** Dimensional sketch showing overall height (up to 12 m) and where the panel and battery box sit along the pole.
- **Dimensioned Flange and Bolt Drawing:** Base-plate hole span (180–260 mm listed range), hole pattern, and anchor bolt size (M16–M22 included; M24 and non-standard bases require review).
- **Site and Foundation Context:** Confirmation of concrete foundation approval and corridor access conditions.

sections.heading: Frequently Asked Questions on Solar Street Light Erection
paragraphs: **Can a 10 m or 12 m solar street light pole be lifted if the bare pole weighs 210 kg and the panel plus battery weigh 110 kg?** No. The combined assembled weight is 320 kg, which exceeds the 300 kg rated load. A mobile crane or alternative approved method must be used.

**Is a complete solar street light pole approved as a standard configuration?** No. Lifting a complete solar assembly has not been validated as a standard configuration on the source specification sheet, so each solar project requires an assembly weight and drawing review.

articles.title: 85 kg Split Two-Module Pole Lifter: Transport Dimensions and 1–2 Operator Planning Boundaries

articles.description: Detailed breakdown of the 85 kg two-module portable light pole lifter (45 kg hydraulic unit and 40 kg 24 V electrical cabinet) and 1–2 operator site planning boundaries.

sections.heading: Two-Module Architecture for Narrow-Access Lighting Sites
paragraphs: Urban sidewalks, pedestrian promenades, landscaped road medians, and multi-level parking decks often block truck-mounted cranes due to width limits, low overhead clearances, or paved surface load restrictions. The velolev Portable Light Pole Lifter addresses physical transport into these corridors through an 85 kg two-module architecture rather than a single heavy chassis.

According to the confirmed S4 specification sheet, the system separates into a 45 kg hydraulic lifting module and a 40 kg electrical cabinet, with source-sheet packaging dimensions of 650 × 350 × 500 mm. Planning crew allocation and site logistics accurately requires understanding both the module weights and the operator boundary stated in the specification table.

sections.heading: 1. Module Mass, Dimensions, and Component Breakdown
paragraphs: Each module has distinct physical dimensions and functional responsibilities on site:

| Equipment Module | S4 Dimensions | S4 Weight | Listed Sub-Components |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Hydraulic lifting module | 610 × 220 × 220 mm | 45 kg | Hydraulic cylinder, hydraulic valve, oil pump, oil pressure gauge |
| Electrical cabinet | 500 × 300 × 250 mm | 40 kg | Control system, hydraulic pump, 24 V rechargeable battery, current and voltage meters, lift buttons |
| Combined equipment total | Two separate modules | 85 kg | Connected on site at the pole base |
| Source-sheet packaging | 650 × 350 × 500 mm | 85 kg net equipment | Packaging material and gross shipping weight confirmed per order |

sections.heading: 2. Why 1–2 Operators Is Listed Instead of Unconditional Single-Person Operation
paragraphs: In the S4 specification sheet, single-person operation appears only as a conditional introductory note, whereas the authoritative parameter table specifies 1–2 operators. From an engineering and occupational safety standpoint, the equipment should never be marketed or planned as an unconditional one-person job.

Moving a 45 kg hydraulic module and a 40 kg electrical cabinet across curbs, unpaved verges, or slopes, aligning a 12 m class column (up to 300 kg) onto foundation anchor studs, and monitoring overhead airspace clearances generally warrants coordinated two-person handling under site manual-handling and lifting rules. Detailed step-by-step operating sequences and personnel positioning rules remain subject to reviewed operating manuals and site safety plans.

sections.heading: 3. Site Access and Logistics Verification Checklist
paragraphs:
When planning a narrow-access installation in a pedestrian corridor, park, or campus, verify four practical logistics points prior to mobilization:
1. **Transfer Route and Surface Bearing:** Confirm footpath width, gate openings, steps, and paving load limits between vehicle unloading and each pole footing.
2. **Manual-Handling Equipment:** Provide suitable carts, trolleys, or two-person lifting straps for the 45 kg and 40 kg modules in accordance with local safety regulations.
3. **Swing-Arc Clearance:** Even when ground corridors are narrow, confirm that the full 12 m elevation arc clears overhead power lines, tree canopies, and building facades.
4. **Base and Load Envelope:** Verify that each pole stays at or below 300 kg total assembled weight and matches the 180–260 mm flange hole span (or has passed a dimensioned drawing review).

sections.heading: Frequently Asked Questions on 85 kg Modular Transport and Crew Size
paragraphs: **What is the heaviest single module of the velolev portable light pole lifter?** The hydraulic lifting module weighs 45 kg (610 × 220 × 220 mm) and the 24 V electrical cabinet weighs 40 kg (500 × 300 × 250 mm), totaling 85 kg.

**How many operators are required on site?** The specification sheet parameter table lists 1–2 operators. Actual crew size must follow your project safety assessment, manual-handling thresholds, and local lifting supervision rules.

articles.title: When Mobile Cranes Are Still Required: Pole Height Over 12 m, Weight Over 300 kg, and Direct-Burial Limits
articles.seoTitle: When Mobile Cranes Are Required Over 300kg & 12m | velolev
articles.description: Clear engineering exclusion matrix defining when a portable hydraulic light pole lifter cannot be used and a mobile crane or alternative lifting method is mandatory.

sections.heading: Defining Clear Equipment Boundaries Before Mobilization
paragraphs: A portable hydraulic light pole lifter is engineered for a defined operating envelope: 12 m class roadway and area lighting columns with a total assembled weight at or below 300 kg and a reviewed anchor-bolt flange base. Treating a portable lifter as a universal replacement for a mobile truck crane creates serious structural, safety, and schedule risks.

Establishing explicit exclusion rules early in tender review ensures that standard 12 m lighting poles benefit from compact two-module access while heavier, taller, or non-flanged structures remain assigned to appropriately rated crane equipment.

sections.heading: 1. Five Conditions Where a Mobile Crane Is Mandatory
paragraphs: Reject crane-free portable lifting and retain a mobile crane or alternative approved lifting system whenever any of the following conditions exist on your project:

| Exclusion Condition | Portable Lifter Boundary (S4) | Required Action on Site |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Total assembled weight over 300 kg | 300 kg maximum rated load | Use a mobile crane; include pole, bracket, luminaire, and solar battery in weight |
| Pole height over 12 m | 12 m applicable pole class | Use a mobile crane for high-mast, stadium, or tall highway columns |
| Direct-burial (embedment) poles without flange base | Designed for anchor-bolt flange base connection | Use a mobile crane or auger-derrick capable of suspending the shaft in the bore |
| Damaged concrete footing or corroded anchor studs | Requires sound foundation and intact M16–M24 studs | Halt lifting until civil repair and structural inspection are completed |
| Unreviewed non-standard bases or multi-utility poles | 180–260 mm span listed; non-standard bases require drawing review | Do not lift without dimensioned drawing approval or crane assignment |

sections.heading: 2. Mixed-Scope Tenders: Combining Portable Lifters and Cranes
paragraphs: Many municipal lighting upgrades and industrial park packages include a mix of standard 8 m to 12 m street light columns alongside a smaller number of 14 m to 18 m intersection poles or heavy multi-arm structures. Separating the bill of quantities into two work packages avoids forcing either tool outside its safe envelope.

Assign the 12 m class columns (at or below 300 kg with verified flange geometry) to portable hydraulic lifting evaluation, and schedule a mobile crane exclusively for the over-height, over-weight, or direct-burial items. When comparing costs across the portable-eligible subset, enter your own local crane rental and crew rates in the velolev Cost Scenario Calculator without assumed price presets.

sections.heading: 3. Pre-Selection Verification Steps for Project Engineers
paragraphs:
Before finalizing equipment selection on a mixed or borderline project, complete four verification checks:
- **Verify Total Lifted Mass:** Confirm structural drawings for every pole type and sum all attachments to ensure each candidate column is at or below 300 kg.
- **Confirm Base-Plate Interface:** Verify that poles use a bolted flange plate rather than direct earth embedment, and check span (180–260 mm) and bolt size (M16–M24).
- **Submit Non-Standard Drawings:** Non-standard bases require a dimensioned drawing review prior to equipment commitment.
- **Audit Overhead and Ground Safety:** Confirm overhead utility clearances and local lifting governance for every pole location.

sections.heading: Frequently Asked Questions on Crane vs Portable Lifter Limits
paragraphs: **Can the velolev portable lifter install direct-burial poles that go into an excavated hole without a flange plate?** No. The equipment connects to a bolted pole base and foundation anchor studs. Direct-burial poles require a crane or suspended lifting method.

**What happens if a project has 35 poles under 300 kg and 5 poles weighing 380 kg?** Only the 35 poles at or below 300 kg and within the 12 m class can be evaluated for the portable lifter; the five 380 kg poles must be erected with a mobile crane.

articles.seoDescription: Engineering exclusion matrix defining when a portable hydraulic light pole lifter cannot be used and a mobile crane or boom truck remains mandatory.

sections.heading: Why Same-Scope Comparison Matters on Multi-Pole Parking Projects
paragraphs: Commercial parking lots, logistics yards, and university campuses frequently require installing 20 to 60 roadway or area lighting columns in a single phase. When comparing a mobile truck crane against the velolev Portable Light Pole Lifter, accurate budgeting depends on defining an identical work package rather than comparing equipment rental hours alone.

Because velolev operates on a private B2B quotation model without public machine prices or assumed regional currency presets, project estimators enter their own local crane rental rates, crew costs, and project volume into the velolev Cost Scenario Calculator to test sensitivity under transparent formulas.

sections.heading: 1. Same-Scope Work Package Comparison Table (40-Pole Example)
paragraphs: Before entering figures into a project cost model, verify that every candidate pole fits within the 12 m applicable pole class, 300 kg rated load, and 180–260 mm flange hole span (or has passed a dimensioned drawing review), then compare each cost driver across the same activities:

| Project Cost & Scope Item | Mobile Truck Crane Scope | Portable Hydraulic Lifter Scope (S4) |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Site mobilisation & vehicle access | Heavy vehicle travel, outrigger pad setup, and lane or bay closures | 85 kg two-module unit (45 kg hydraulic + 40 kg 24 V cabinet) transported in light service vehicles |
| Equipment rate basis | Daily or hourly crane hire plus minimum mobilisation charges | Enter your quoted equipment basis in the calculator; no public price is assumed |
| Crew allocation | Crane operator plus rigging and ground crew per site rules | 1–2 operators listed on specification sheet; align staffing with site safety plan |
| Lifting & alignment workflow | Overhead boom suspension from delivery trailer to anchor bolts | Ground-level base connection and hydraulic lift for reviewed flange bases |
| Non-lifting activities | Pole unloading, luminaire wiring, plumbing, and anchor nut tightening | Same unloading, wiring, plumbing, and anchor nut tightening scope applies |

sections.heading: 2. Isolating Out-of-Scope Columns Before Modeling Costs
paragraphs: In many parking lot and perimeter road packages, most columns are 8 m to 12 m light poles under 300 kg, while a small subset of perimeter floodlight poles exceed 12 m or 300 kg. Exclude over-height and over-weight columns from the portable lifter subset and keep a mobile crane budgeted for those specific foundations.
Additionally, review the Cost Scenario Calculator edge conditions: the tool models direct operating comparison without assumed resale value, and zero project volume returns zero lifting activity.

sections.heading: 3. Preparing a Parking Lot Project Brief for Quotation
paragraphs:
When requesting a private B2B quotation for a multi-pole parking or campus project, include four factual inputs:
1. **Pole Schedule:** Total pole count, pole height (up to 12 m class), and total assembled weight including bracket and luminaire (at or below 300 kg).
2. **Base-Plate & Bolt Details:** Flange hole span (180–260 mm listed range), hole pattern (4, 6, or 8 holes), and anchor bolt diameter (M16–M22 included; M24 and non-standard bases require drawing review).
3. **Site Access & Layout:** Pavement clearances, underground parking deck load limits, and overhead utility lines.
4. **Destination & Delivery Terms:** Project country, port or site destination, and target delivery schedule.

paragraphs: **Why does the velolev Cost Scenario Calculator leave equipment price blank?** velolev quotes B2B export configurations privately based on project scope and destination, so no public equipment price or regional currency preset is published.

**Does the 20 s manufacturer-reported lift time represent full installation time per pole?** No. The 20 s figure refers only to the reported lift stroke (with field validation pending). Full per-pole cycle time must include transport, staging, wiring, alignment, and anchor tightening.

articles.title: 24 V Battery Portable Pole Lifter for Off-Grid Rural Roads: Lifts Per Charge and Field Planning
articles.seoTitle: 24V Battery Pole Lifter for Off-Grid Rural Roads | velolev
articles.description: Field planning guide for using the 24 V rechargeable battery electrical cabinet on off-grid rural highway corridors, including manufacturer-reported lifts per charge boundaries.

sections.heading: Self-Contained 24 V Power for Unpowered Highway Corridors
paragraphs: Rural road lighting and off-grid solar corridor projects often span kilometers of highway where grid power is unavailable during civil and mechanical installation. Bringing a separate diesel generator alongside lifting gear adds fuel logistics, noise, and extra vehicle movements.

The velolev Portable Light Pole Lifter integrates a 24 V rechargeable battery inside its 40 kg electrical cabinet (500 × 300 × 250 mm), enabling hydraulic lifting strokes without external mains electricity. Proper field planning requires separating confirmed battery hardware specs from manufacturer-reported endurance figures that remain under field validation.

sections.heading: 1. 24 V Electrical Cabinet Specifications and Evidence Status
paragraphs: Review the exact S4 specification parameters for the power and control module before scheduling multi-day rural shifts:

| Power & Endurance Parameter | S4 Specification Value | Evidence Classification & Planning Rule |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Power supply voltage | 24 V rechargeable battery | Confirmed S4 specification; housed inside the electrical cabinet |
| Electrical cabinet weight & size | 40 kg · 500 × 300 × 250 mm | Confirmed S4 specification; contains control system, pump, battery, ammeter, voltmeter, and lift buttons |
| Lifts per full charge | Over 50 lifts per full charge | Manufacturer-reported; field validation pending — treat as nominal planning reference |
| Lift stroke duration | 20 s reported lift time | Manufacturer-reported; field validation pending — excludes setup and tightening |
| Usage cycle rating | Over 3000 usage cycles | Manufacturer-reported; field validation pending — not a warranty or load-curve guarantee |

sections.heading: 2. Practical Charging and Shift Planning on Remote Routes
paragraphs: Because the over 50 lifts per full charge metric is manufacturer-reported with field validation still pending, site supervisors should build conservative charging buffers into rural deployment schedules rather than running batteries to depletion miles from a depot.

Plan overnight recharging at the site compound or support camp, monitor the onboard current and voltage meters on the electrical cabinet throughout the shift, and confirm charger voltage compatibility with your local depot power supply when requesting a quotation.

sections.heading: 3. Combined Checks for Off-Grid Rural Pole Installations
paragraphs:
Power independence is only one requirement for rural road lighting. Before mobilizing to an off-grid corridor, verify three companion checks:
- **Complete Assembly Weight:** Confirm that every pole, outreach arm, luminaire, and solar module stays at or below the 300 kg rated load and within the 12 m pole class.
- **Base Flange & Anchor Studs:** Confirm 180–260 mm flange hole span and M16–M24 anchor bolt sizes (M16–M22 included; M24 and non-standard bases require drawing review).
- **Soil and Verge Bearing:** Ensure the shoulder or unpaved verge adjacent to the concrete foundation provides stable footing for the equipment and 1–2 operators.

sections.heading: Frequently Asked Questions on 24 V Battery Operation
paragraphs: **Does the velolev portable lifter require a generator on off-grid sites?** No. The electrical cabinet houses a 24 V rechargeable battery that powers the hydraulic pump during lifting.

**Has the over 50 lifts per full charge figure been independently verified in field trials?** Not yet. The source specification sheet lists over 50 lifts per full charge as a manufacturer-reported figure with field validation pending.

sections.heading: Transporting Pole Lifting Equipment Without Flatbed Trucks
paragraphs: Contractors maintaining municipal street lighting, park pathways, and campus parking lots frequently operate standard utility pickup trucks or service vans rather than flatbed crane trucks. Knowing exact module dimensions and net weights allows logistics planners to verify cargo-bed fitment and tie-down points before dispatch.
The velolev Portable Light Pole Lifter has a combined equipment weight of 85 kg split across two modules, with source-sheet packaging dimensions of 650 × 350 × 500 mm.

sections.heading: 1. Dimensional & Mass Reference Table for Vehicle Loading
paragraphs: Use the confirmed S4 dimensions below when checking cargo bed clearance, van door height, or freight palletization:

| Item / Sub-Assembly | Length × Width × Height (mm) | Weight | Logistics & Handling Note |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Hydraulic lifting module | 610 × 220 × 220 mm | 45 kg | Compact footprint; secure against rolling or sliding in transit |
| Electrical cabinet (24 V) | 500 × 300 × 250 mm | 40 kg | Keep upright and protected from moisture and impact during transport |
| Combined unboxed equipment | Two separate modules | 85 kg total | Can be carried separately from vehicle to pedestrian work zone |
| Source-sheet packaging | 650 × 350 × 500 mm | 85 kg net equipment | Packaging material and gross shipping weight confirmed per actual order |

sections.heading: 2. What Is Confirmed vs Confirmed Per Order in Shipping Specs
paragraphs: To prevent tender or freight-forwarding misunderstandings, distinguish what is fixed in the S4 specification sheet from order-specific shipping details. The 650 × 350 × 500 mm packaging dimensions and 85 kg equipment weight are confirmed source-sheet values.

However, outer crate construction material, gross packed shipping weight, and export wood-treatment markings are not fixed in the S4 sheet and are confirmed per actual order when preparing your destination quotation.

sections.heading: 3. Vehicle-to-Foundation Transfer Checklist
paragraphs:
Once the pickup truck or van reaches the nearest vehicular drop-off point, verify four site-transfer details:
1. **Crew & Handling Aids:** Follow the 1–2 operator specification boundary and use appropriate carts or two-person lifting techniques for the 45 kg and 40 kg modules.
2. **Included Hardware Kit:** Verify that the 4 sets each of M16, M18, M20, and M22 anchor bolts and 1 set of ground stakes are accounted for prior to leaving the depot.
3. **Gate & Curb Clearances:** Confirm pedestrian path widths and surface load limits between the parking bay and each foundation.
4. **Pole & Flange Envelope:** Confirm poles do not exceed 12 m height or 300 kg total assembled weight and match reviewed flange drawings.

sections.heading: Frequently Asked Questions on Transport and Packaging
paragraphs: **What are the packaging dimensions of the velolev portable light pole lifter?** The source specification sheet lists packaging dimensions of 650 × 350 × 500 mm and a total equipment weight of 85 kg.
**Are packaging material and gross shipping weight fixed on the specification sheet?** No. Packaging material and gross weight are confirmed per actual order based on shipping mode and destination.

articles.title: Planning 10 m and 12 m Street Light Pole Erection Near Overhead Power Lines and Narrow Alleys
articles.seoTitle: Pole Erection Near Overhead Lines & Narrow Alleys | velolev
articles.description: Pre-installation site survey checklist for evaluating ground-level hydraulic pole erection near overhead distribution lines, facades, and narrow urban alleys.

sections.heading: Why Constrained Urban Corridors Require Two-Plane Clearance Checks
paragraphs: Retrofitting street lighting in historic districts, narrow residential lanes, and tree-lined avenues presents two simultaneous geometric constraints: narrow ground corridors that block crane outriggers, and overhead utility wires or building projections that intersect a 10 m to 12 m pole swing radius.

While the 85 kg two-module velolev Portable Light Pole Lifter (45 kg hydraulic module plus 40 kg electrical cabinet) resolves ground-level vehicle access, ground portability never overrides electrical approach clearances or municipal lifting permits.

sections.heading: 1. Pre-Installation Corridor & Airspace Survey Matrix
paragraphs: Document these five site parameters for your licensed site supervisor and local utility authority before selecting an erection method:

| Site Constraint Dimension | What to Measure on Site | Engineering & Governance Boundary |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Overhead conductor height & lateral offset | Vertical and horizontal distance from foundation to nearest energized line | Must satisfy local utility minimum approach distances across full 12 m arc |
| Ground corridor width & surface | Narrowest gate, alley, or sidewalk bottleneck and paving condition | Must accommodate 610 × 220 × 220 mm and 500 × 300 × 250 mm modules safely |
| Horizontal staging laydown length | Unobstructed ground length along the axis of pole assembly | Pole shaft, bracket arm, and luminaire require level pre-lift assembly space |
| Adjacent facades, trees, and signage | Lateral clearance within the pole tip swing envelope | Prevent contact during elevation from horizontal to vertical |
| Base plate & foundation geometry | Flange hole span (180–260 mm), bolt diameter (M16–M24), and footing condition | Non-standard bases require a dimensioned drawing review |

sections.heading: 2. Planning Guidance vs Site Operating Procedures
paragraphs: Consistent with velolev editorial and engineering policy, this guide supports early project planning and site data collection rather than serving as a field operating manual. Detailed step-by-step operating sequences, personnel exclusion zones, and electrical isolation protocols must be governed by reviewed equipment manuals, certified supervisors, and local electrical safety regulations.

sections.heading: 3. Information to Attach When Requesting a Constrained-Site Review
paragraphs:
If you are evaluating crane-free installation for a narrow alley or utility-adjacent street lighting project, include four items in your quotation request:
- **Pole Height & Assembled Weight:** Confirm column height (up to 12 m class) and complete weight including luminaire and bracket (at or below 300 kg).
- **Dimensioned Flange Drawing:** Provide hole count, span definition, and anchor bolt diameter (M16–M22 included; M24 requires separate confirmation).
- **Corridor Site Photographs:** Include photos showing foundation surroundings, alley width, and overhead utility lines.
- **Crew & Safety Governance:** Plan staffing within the 1–2 operator specification listing and local lifting supervision rules.

sections.heading: Frequently Asked Questions on Narrow-Alley and Overhead-Line Projects
paragraphs: **Does compact 85 kg equipment allow lifting directly underneath low overhead power lines?** No. Regardless of lifting equipment size, the 10 m or 12 m pole tip must maintain mandatory electrical safety clearances approved by the responsible utility and site safety engineer.

**Can this article be used as a step-by-step field rigging manual?** No. It is a pre-installation planning guide; step-by-step site operating sequences require reviewed operating documentation and site-specific safety supervision.

articles.seoDescription: Pre-lift planning and clearance checks for 10m and 12m street light pole installation near overhead power lines, tight easements, and pedestrian alleys.

articles.title: 20-Second Reported Lift Stroke vs Total Street Light Pole Installation Time: Scope Breakdown
articles.seoTitle: 20s Lift Stroke vs Total Pole Installation Time | velolev
articles.description: Understand the difference between the manufacturer-reported 20 s hydraulic lift stroke (field validation pending) and full per-pole installation hours on street lighting sites.

sections.heading: Separating Hydraulic Stroke Duration from Full Installation Cycle Time
paragraphs: The velolev Portable Light Pole Lifter specification sheet lists a manufacturer-reported lift time of 20 s alongside over 50 lifts per full charge and more than 3000 usage cycles. In project scheduling and tender estimation, mistaking a 20 s hydraulic elevation stroke for total per-pole installation time leads to unrealistic crew productivity targets.

As documented in the velolev editorial policy and product specification baseline, all three performance figures are manufacturer-reported labels with field validation pending—and lifting time is never a statement of complete installation time.

sections.heading: 1. Complete Street Light Pole Installation Activity Breakdown
paragraphs: A realistic per-pole schedule accounts for every sequential activity from pole staging to final sign-off:

| Installation Stage | Key Site Activities | Relationship to S4 Specification Sheet |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 1. Logistics & module positioning | Move 45 kg hydraulic unit and 40 kg 24 V cabinet to footing; check foundation and studs | Governed by site layout and 1–2 operator manual-handling plan |
| 2. Ground-level pole dress-out | Fit outreach bracket arm, LED luminaire(s), internal wiring, and solar components | Must verify total assembled weight stays at or below 300 kg |
| 3. Base connection & alignment | Mate pole base to lifting assembly and align with foundation anchor bolts | Must match reviewed flange drawing and 180–260 mm span |
| 4. Hydraulic lift stroke | Raise 12 m class pole from horizontal to vertical position | 20 s figure on S4 sheet is manufacturer-reported; field validation pending |
| 5. Plumbing, nut tightening & electrical termination | Tighten structural anchor nuts, verify plumbness, disconnect lifter, and terminate cables | Essential post-lift work not included in hydraulic stroke time |

sections.heading: 2. How to Use Performance Figures Responsibly in Schedules and Cost Models
paragraphs: When building a project schedule or comparing methods in the Cost Scenario Calculator, estimate total daily pole output based on your crew size (1–2 operators listed on the sheet), distance between foundations, ground-level wiring complexity, and local inspection steps.

Treat the 20 s lift time, over 50 lifts per charge, and more than 3000 usage cycles strictly as manufacturer-reported specification figures pending field validation rather than guaranteed cycle-time or service-life commitments.

sections.heading: 3. Verification Questions to Include in Your Project Inquiry
paragraphs:
If your project schedule depends on daily pole completion targets, include four practical context details when submitting `/quote/`:
- **Total Pole Quantity & Spacing:** Number of poles and average distance between foundations.
- **Pre-Assembly Scope:** Whether luminaires and brackets are pre-assembled on the ground before lifting.
- **Assembled Pole Weight & Height:** Exact total mass (up to 300 kg) and column height (up to 12 m class).
- **Flange & Anchor Bolt Details:** Bolt diameter (M16–M24) and dimensioned base drawing for non-standard flanges.

sections.heading: Frequently Asked Questions on Lift Time and Output
paragraphs: **Has the 20 s lift time been verified across different pole weights in independent field tests?** Not yet. The 20 s value is listed on the S4 specification sheet as manufacturer-reported with field validation pending.

**Does more than 3000 usage cycles represent a formal warranty period?** No. More than 3000 usage cycles is a manufacturer-reported specification label with field validation pending, not a warranty or load-curve guarantee.

articles.title: Pre-Installation Foundation and Anchor Stud Inspection Checklist Before Pole Lifter Review
articles.seoTitle: Foundation & Anchor Stud Pre-Lift Checklist | velolev
articles.description: What foundation dimensions, anchor bolt measurements, and site photographs to gather before submitting a street light pole connection review.

sections.heading: Why Foundation Condition Governs Base-Anchored Pole Lifting
paragraphs: Unlike a mobile crane that suspends a lighting column from above, a ground-level portable hydraulic pole lifter connects at the pole base and transfers erection reactions directly into the concrete foundation and embedded anchor studs.

Submitting accurate foundation measurements and photographs before mobilization ensures that incompatible stud sizes, unreviewed flange patterns, or damaged concrete footings are identified during engineering review rather than on site.

sections.heading: 1. Pre-Review Foundation and Anchor Bolt Data Table
paragraphs: Record and verify these five foundation items before completing the FlangeChecker or sending a drawing to `/quote/`:

| Foundation Check Item | What to Measure or Photograph | Compatibility & Review Boundary |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Anchor bolt thread diameter | Measure nominal stud diameter (M16, M18, M20, M22, M24, or other) | M16–M22 included (4 sets each); M24 listed but not included by default |
| Anchor bolt pattern & count | Count total embedded studs (4, 6, or 8 bolts) | 4-hole pattern in quick check; 6-hole or 8-hole bases require drawing review |
| Flange hole span & drawing definition | Measure hole-to-hole span and check how the drawing defines it | 180–260 mm listed range; verify measurement definition against drawing |
| Thread condition & projection | Inspect threads for corrosion/damage and measure exposed length above concrete | Damaged or bent studs must be repaired and approved before any lift |
| Concrete footing sign-off | Confirm civil completion and structural approval by responsible site engineer | Equipment review does not replace civil foundation engineering approval |

sections.heading: 2. Distinguishing Pre-Inquiry Checks from Site Engineering Instructions
paragraphs: Civil foundation design—including concrete mix strength, curing schedule, reinforcement cage depth, and base-plate grouting tolerances—must always be specified and signed off by the project civil or structural engineer.

velolev reviews equipment-to-flange mechanical compatibility based on your dimensioned drawings and S4 equipment specifications; it does not issue civil foundation design approvals or field installation manuals.

sections.heading: 3. Four-Item Photo and Drawing Package for Fast Connection Review
paragraphs:
Attach the following package when requesting a connection review through `/quote/`:
1. **Dimensioned Base-Plate Drawing:** Show plate outer dimensions, hole count, hole diameter, and labeled hole span.
2. **Foundation Top Plan:** Show embedded anchor bolt layout and confirm that stud positions match the pole base plate.
3. **Close-Up Stud Photographs:** Clear photos of the concrete pedestal top and anchor bolt threads.
4. **Assembled Pole Summary:** Confirm total weight (at or below 300 kg) and pole height (up to 12 m class).

sections.heading: Frequently Asked Questions on Foundation Readiness
paragraphs: **Does passing the online 180–260 mm quick check approve my concrete foundation?** No. The quick check only compares your entered span and bolt size against the listed S4 equipment range. Foundation structural adequacy must be approved by your project engineer.

**What if my anchor bolts are M24 on a 4-hole base with a 240 mm span?** M24 is listed in the compatibility table, but M24 hardware is not included in the standard kit. Submit your dimensioned drawing so hardware and fitment can be reviewed.

articles.seoDescription: Pre-installation checklist for concrete foundation cure strength, anchor bolt projection, thread inspection, and base plate orientation checks.

articles.title: Evaluating Portable Light Pole Lifter Technical Documentation in B2B Tenders: Source Specs vs Pending Records
articles.seoTitle: Evaluating Pole Lifter Specs in B2B Tenders | velolev
articles.description: Transparent procurement guide distinguishing confirmed S4 specification data, manufacturer-reported metrics, and project-specific compliance documents in B2B tenders.

sections.heading: Why Evidence Transparency Matters in Municipal and EPC Tenders
paragraphs: Public lighting tenders, utility framework contracts, and EPC procurement packages require technical submittals to distinguish verified product specifications from pending test reports or order-specific certificates. Overstating unverified claims exposes contractors to tender disqualification and site compliance delays.

velolev structures all public product information around a controlled specification baseline (S4, version 2026-10-28.3) and explicitly marks which items are confirmed specifications, manufacturer-reported figures, or project-specific records pending verification.

sections.heading: 1. Technical Evidence Classification Matrix for Tender Reviewers
paragraphs: Use this four-tier evidence matrix when compiling a technical submittal or pre-qualification file:

| Documentation / Evidence Category | Current Status on velolev | How Procurement Teams Should Use It |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| S4 specification sheet facts | Confirmed product source (12 m class, 300 kg load, 24 V, 85 kg split modules, 180–260 mm span, M16–M22 kit) | Download structured JSON and CSV files from /resources/ for technical comparison tables |
| Manufacturer-reported performance | Listed on S4 (20 s lift time, over 50 lifts/charge, more than 3000 cycles) with field validation pending | Cite with explicit qualification that independent field validation is pending |
| Project information worksheet | Public downloadable template on /resources/ | Use to standardize pole weight, flange drawing, and site data before requesting review |
| Certificates, field manual, warranty, and case records | Not published as generic downloads; confirmed or supplied per actual order/review | State specific tender compliance requirements in your /quote/ inquiry |

sections.heading: 2. Aligning Equipment Review with Tender Submittal Stages
paragraphs: During early tender budgeting, engineers can use the public specification summary, FlangeChecker, and Cost Scenario Calculator (with your own local crane and labor rates) to screen whether portable hydraulic lifting fits the 12 m / 300 kg project subset.

Before binding equipment procurement, submit dimensioned flange drawings, complete assembled pole weights, and destination compliance requirements through `/quote/` so configuration compatibility and order documentation can be confirmed privately.

sections.heading: 3. Summary of Hard Commercial and Technical Boundaries
paragraphs:
Tender evaluators reviewing velolev documentation should note four clear boundaries:
- **Single Physical Product:** One portable hydraulic light pole lifter system (`modelNumber: null`), evaluated across project-specific flange and load conditions.
- **No Unreviewed Operating Manuals:** Step-by-step site operating sequences are held for reviewed documentation rather than published as generic web instructions.
- **Complete Solar Assemblies Pending Validation:** Solar street light projects require full assembled weight and geometry review.
- **Private B2B Quotation:** Equipment pricing, packaging material, gross shipping weight, and warranty terms are confirmed per actual order.

sections.heading: Frequently Asked Questions on Tender Documentation
paragraphs: **Where can I download machine-readable product specifications for a tender comparison table?** Visit `/resources/` to download the source-derived JSON and CSV specification summaries alongside the blank project information worksheet.

**Are third-party compliance certificates or installation SOPs available for instant public download?** No. Those records are not published as generic downloads; specify your project documentation requirements when submitting an inquiry.

articles.title: Solar Street Light Wind Sail Area and Site Exposure Inputs for Pre-Installation Engineering Review
articles.seoTitle: Solar Street Light Wind Sail Area & Site Assessment | velolev
articles.description: How to document solar panel surface area, mounting elevation, terrain exposure, and total assembled weight under 300 kg for pre-installation engineering review.

sections.heading: Why Solar Panel Surface Area Affects Erection Planning
paragraphs: Large photovoltaic modules mounted near the top of a 10 m to 12 m lighting column introduce both extra static mass and an elevated wind sail area compared with a compact LED luminaire alone. Even when ambient site conditions appear calm at ground level, wind pressure acting on a broad solar panel at 10 m to 12 m height creates overturning reactions at the pole base.

Because lifting a complete solar street light assembly has not yet been validated as a standard configuration on the velolev specification sheet, recording accurate panel geometry and site exposure data is essential for pre-installation engineering review.

sections.heading: 1. Solar Sail-Area and Site Exposure Submittal Table
paragraphs: Include these five geometric and site parameters in your solar project worksheet before requesting an equipment review:

| Solar & Site Input | What to Measure and Document | Why It Matters in Engineering Review |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Photovoltaic panel dimensions & count | Length, width, thickness, and number of panels on the top frame | Defines effective wind sail area and eccentric offset at column top |
| Panel tilt angle and orientation | Fixed tilt angle and azimuth relative to prevailing site wind | Affects projected wind area during and immediately after erection |
| Battery enclosure size & mounting height | Box dimensions, mass, and attachment height on the shaft | Contributes both top-heavy mass and secondary wind drag |
| Complete assembled system weight | Pole shaft + panel(s) + frame + battery box + luminaire | Must remain at or below the 300 kg rated load and 12 m pole class |
| Corridor terrain exposure | Open coastal plain, rural highway embankment, or sheltered urban street | Helps site engineers establish safe weather governance rules |

sections.heading: 2. Weather Governance Without Unverified Wind-Speed Thresholds
paragraphs: The current S4 product specification sheet does not publish a numeric operating wind-speed cutoff. Rather than relying on arbitrary or unverified wind numbers, site supervisors must enforce local lifting governance, monitor real-time weather forecasts, and halt lifting immediately whenever wind conditions affect column stability.

When top-mounted solar sail areas, total weight (above 300 kg), or pole height (above 12 m) exceed portable equipment boundaries, assign the installation to a mobile crane or alternative approved method.

sections.heading: 3. Step-by-Step Solar Project Review Preparation
paragraphs:
Prepare a complete solar project file before submitting `/quote/?context=solar-assembly`:
- **Verify Assembled Weight:** Confirm itemized component weights sum to 300 kg or less.
- **Attach Dimensional Drawings:** Provide both the upper solar bracket elevation drawing and the lower base-plate flange drawing (180–260 mm span, M16–M24 bolts).
- **Confirm Foundation Approval:** Verify civil engineer sign-off on the concrete footing and anchor bolts.
- **Document Off-Grid Logistics:** Note pole count, spacing, and charging access for the 24 V electrical cabinet.

sections.heading: Frequently Asked Questions on Solar Panel Sail Area and Lifting
paragraphs: **Does the velolev specification sheet list a maximum wind speed for lifting solar poles?** No. No numeric wind-speed threshold is published in the S4 specification sheet. Lifting operations must follow site weather governance and project engineering review.
**What if the solar panel and battery push the total pole weight to 315 kg?** A 315 kg assembly exceeds the 300 kg rated load and cannot be lifted with this equipment; a mobile crane must be used.

articles.seoDescription: Assess solar panel wind sail area, aerodynamic drag, foundation overturning moments, and gust exposure before crane-free street light pole erection.
